questions.q: What is the basic economic problem?
questions.why: Scarcity forces choices about what to produce, how and for whom.

questions.q: Opportunity cost is…
o: the money price of a good
the next best alternative given up
questions.why: Choosing one option means losing the benefit of the next best.

questions.q: A shift outwards of a production possibility curve shows…
questions.why: More or better resources let the economy produce more of both goods.

questions.q: If the price of a good rises, what happens to the quantity demanded?
questions.why: A movement along the demand curve, not a shift.

questions.q: Which causes the demand curve for tea to shift right?
o: A fall in the price of tea
A rise in the price of coffee (a substitute)
A rise in the price of tea
questions.why: A dearer substitute makes people switch to tea at every price.

questions.q: Price elasticity of demand is −0.5. Demand is…
questions.why: Its value is less than 1 (ignoring the sign), so quantity changes less than price.

questions.q: A maximum price set below the equilibrium price causes…
questions.why: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the lower price.

questions.q: A merit good is…
o: beneficial and underconsumed in a free market
questions.why: Examples are education and healthcare; people underestimate their benefits.

questions.q: What is the main function of a central bank?
o: Issuing currency and setting interest rates
questions.why: It controls monetary policy and acts as the government's and banks' bank.

questions.q: Division of labour means…
questions.why: Specialisation raises productivity but can make work repetitive.

questions.q: Total revenue is…
questions.why: Profit = total revenue − total cost.

questions.q: Which is a macroeconomic aim of government?
questions.why: Aims include growth, low unemployment, stable prices, a sustainable balance of payments and fair income distribution.

questions.q: A progressive tax…
o: takes the same percentage from everyone
takes a larger percentage from higher incomes
takes a smaller percentage from higher incomes
questions.why: Income tax with rising rates is an example.

questions.q: Inflation is measured in many countries using…
questions.why: A CPI tracks the price of a weighted basket of goods and services.

questions.q: Cutting interest rates is likely to…
questions.why: Cheaper borrowing encourages consumption and investment.

questions.q: Which indicator combines income, education and life expectancy?
questions.why: The Human Development Index measures more than income.

questions.q: Absolute poverty means…
o: not having enough for basic needs
questions.why: Relative poverty compares income with others in the country.

questions.q: A tariff is…
questions.why: Quotas limit quantity; tariffs raise import prices.

questions.q: If a country's currency depreciates, its exports become…
questions.why: Foreign buyers need less of their currency to buy the same goods.

questions.q: A current account deficit means…
o: exports of goods and services exceed imports
imports of goods and services exceed exports
questions.why: The current account mainly records trade in goods and services plus income flows.
